text:
Ravi: heads up — after the kernel-routing tweak rolled at 02:15 UTC we're getting a slow-but-steady GPU mem climb on continuous batching canaries, ends in OOM on p3-small :thinking_face:
Maya: saw the alerts, looking at the KV cache shadowing telemetry. growth looks correlated with batches that have many short seqs (lots of padding)
Jordan: could be fragmentation + padding compounding. do we have a recent heap dump/allocator profile? :mag:
Sam: i grabbed a trace on canary-3, attaching the rough numbers below
Sam: ```
-- sample (canary-3, 02:43)
batch: 32 requests, seqs: [16, 8, 256, 32, 8, 8, ...]
allocator: free slabs: 120 -> 86
workspace_allocs: +1.8GB
KV cache pinned: +0.4GB
mem_before: 10.9G
mem_after: 13.1G
oom when next big seq hit (~+3GB)
```
Noah: interesting that KV only 400MB but workspace blow is 1.8GB. implies per-seq temp buffers / padding burn, not just KV shadowing
Maya: i reran with continuous batching disabled (drop-in flag) and memory stabilizes. so batching heuristics change kernel selection and that seems to influence workspace sizing heuristics
Ravi: kernel switch path picks fp16/quant kernel variant that tries to preallocate a workspace based on max-seq-in-batch. if padding distribution is skewed we allocate as if all are max. cheap for throughput, expensive for this workload
Jordan: two hypotheses: 1) allocator fragmentation prevents reusing smaller freed slabs, 2) workspace accounting uses conservative max instead of live-needed. either could cause the observed climb
Sam: quick experiment: reduced workspace margin from 1.2x -> 1.0x on canary-2. result: no immediate OOM but perf stable? small reg in throughput (~2% drop).
Maya: can we implement a coalescing pass on free lists (merge adjacent slabs) and a compacting fallback when free memory < threshold? that should reduce frag. but compaction costs latency spikes
Noah: also consider changing batching scoring to prefer grouping similar seq-lens (minimizes max-padding) — cheap immediate win for these traffic patterns
Jordan: i ran jemalloc-like fragmentation metrics. free-extent-count increased steadily between allocations, indicating we’re leaking small fragments. attaching snippet:
Jordan: ```
frag_metrics: total_free_extents: 142 -> 218
avg_free_size: 48KB -> 31KB
external_frag_ratio: 0.18 -> 0.34
```
Ravi: ok action plan suggestion: 1) revert kernel-routing canary until we push allocator coalesce + tighter workspace sizing, 2) add batching grouping heuristic to reduce padding, 3) add periodic compaction on low-qps nodes, 4) add more granular telemetry (per-seq workspace delta)
Sam: i've opened a PR with a conservative coalesce pass + workspace reuse hint, it's behind feature flag: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1729 :eyes:
Maya: running Sam's branch on canary-4 now, will report mem curve in 30m
Noah: i'll add a metric: workspace_delta_per_seq and expose on console per-route so we can detect high pad burn workloads automatically
Jordan: for the immediate revert, infra-bot can schedule a rollback. infra-bot: can you queue the route rollback for the kernel-routing change on canary?
infra-bot: scheduled rollback for kernel-routing -> 02:55 UTC, canary-1/2/3 targeted. status: queued
Ravi: thanks. follow-ups: Sam + Jordan to iterate allocator coalesce (PR feedback), Maya to run A/B on batching-group heuristic, Noah to add metric + alert. sync in #eng-runtime in 1h. :thumbsup:
Maya: FYI i also noticed a small perf regression in one of the quant kernels when reuse is aggressive — need to balance reuse vs kernel-specific alignment constraints
Sam: noted, i'll add alignment guards to reuse logic
Noah: if this stabilizes, we should convert the workspace_metric into an Optimize recommendation for customers: flag workloads with high padding burn and suggest grouping/quantization profile
Ravi: perfect. good triage everyone. recording this thread into the incident/ops notes.
